He instructed diplomats to prioritize securing weapons and air defense systems for Ukraine. by Kyiv Post | Aug. 3, 2026, 3:45 pm Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Patriot systems of the Defence Ground-Based Air Defense Command (DGAC) of the Dutch air defense forces prepare for departure to Poland where they will deploy to secure NATO's eastern border airspace for six months, at Vredepeel air base on November 19, 2025. (Photo by Sem van der Wal / ANP / AFP) / Netherlands OUT Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip Ukrainian ambassadors will help advance Europe’s Freyja anti-ballistic defense program and negotiate new international drone agreements as Kyiv expands diplomatic efforts to strengthen the country’s defense President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday. In a meeting with Ukrainian ambassadors, Zelensky said diplomatic missions must prioritize defense cooperation. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . “An ambassador must know how many air defense missiles the country where they serve has and how to ensure those missiles are in our launchers rather than sitting in warehouses,” he said. The project, known as FREYJA, is the centerpiece of the newly created Integrated Anti-Ballistic Missile Coalition, launched by Ukraine and several European countries to develop a joint missile defense capability. Advertisement The system is designed to detect, track and intercept ballistic missiles, including threats similar to Russia’s Iskander and Kinzhal missiles. It is expected to complement existing Western systems such as the US-made Patriot and France-Italy’s SAMP/T, rather than replace them. Ukraine is expected to play a central role in the project by developing the interceptor missile – the key component needed to destroy incoming ballistic threats. Ukrainian defense company Fire Point is working on the FP-7.X interceptor missile, which is being designed specifically for air defense missions rather than ground strikes. Other Topics of Interest Russia Captured More Territory Than Ukraine Reclaimed in July, DeepState Reports Ukraine’s Defense Forces reduced the area of Russian-occupied territory, with 25 square kilometers attributed in May and 27 square kilometers in June. The project brings together Ukraine and European partners including Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Spain, Sweden and the United Kingdom. Zelensky said every Ukrainian ambassador is expected to work on securing military assistance. “You must bring weapons. This must become a key performance indicator for our embassies,” he said. The president added that Ukrainian diplomats will also contribute to work on the Freya anti-ballistic defense project in Europe and help negotiate new agreements on drone cooperation with international partners. Advertisement Other priorities for diplomats Beyond defense cooperation, Zelensky instructed ambassadors to strengthen efforts to protect Ukrainians abroad from xenophobia and to maintain regular visits to Ukraine. He also called for deeper cooperation with key international partners, including the United States, Japan, India, and China. Russia attacked Ukraine in Saturday’s early hours with 35 missiles and 185 drones , killing at least nine people and injuring 30 more. Due to a critical shortage of Patriot interceptors, Ukrainian air defenses were only able to shoot down one ballistic missile . The strikes affected seven districts in Kyiv, damaging 18 residential buildings, educational facilities, and the Lithuanian embassy. Attacks also targeted the Dnipropetrovsk, Sumy, Kharkiv, and Poltava regions. Zelensky urged international partners to expedite air defense deliveries to mitigate further casualties. The European Union’s ambassador to Ukraine, Katarína Mathernová, told the outlet that the group would meet twice weekly over the coming months to accelerate the work. The joint task force brings Ukrainian and European Commission officials together around the interim benchmarks that Kyiv must meet as negotiations advance. Its creation follows Hungary’s removal of objections that had held up talks on the EU’s internal market and on competitiveness and inclusive growth. Those two negotiating clusters opened October 13, bringing Ukraine’s total to four out of six. Kyiv is seeking to open the remaining two before the end of the year, according to Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha’s remarks reported by Kyiv Post. That is a Ukrainian objective; completing membership negotiations still requires reforms and further decisions by EU governments. The task force’s immediate assignment Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos said she had discussed the next steps with Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi and agreed to form the group, according to reports by Euronews and the Kyiv Independent. The latter reported that President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told EU leaders the group had been established the previous day. The practical work concerns outstanding requirements on the fundamentals of accession, including the rule of law and efforts against corruption. Euronews reported that a Commission official described the arrangement as following a model used for Montenegro and Moldova. Ukraine is also expected to receive a roadmap and an indicative timetable as part of an enlargement package anticipated in early November, the outlet reported. Those are expected next steps in the accession process, with the task force intended to help Ukrainian officials complete the required work. A diplomatic opening with Budapest The new mechanism emerged during a week of renewed contacts between Kyiv and Budapest. Zelenskyy and Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar agreed during talks in Brussels on Friday to work toward normalizing relations, Kyiv Post reported. Sybiha described cooperation covering politics, the economy and humanitarian affairs. Magyar said discussions would continue at ministerial level. Possible further talks in Berehove, a center of Ukraine’s Hungarian community, were under consideration. Zelenskyy also received an invitation to Budapest for the October 23 commemoration of Hungary’s 1956 revolution, deputy presidential chief of staff Ihor Zhovkva told Euronews, according to Kyiv Post. The president was considering attending; the report did not confirm a visit. Education changes preceded the new talks Ukraine’s parliament adopted education amendments October 12, and Zelenskyy signed them that day, according to Kyiv Post and Euronews. The legislation expands protections for national minorities whose languages have official status in the EU. Ukrainian remains the state language of education . Euronews reported that the changes create a special legal status for qualifying minority-language schools and expand the use of eligible languages in school activities and communications. They also add protections for native-language education when schools are reorganized or closed. Kyiv Post’s account described provisions allowing certain school documents and signs to be duplicated in the relevant minority language. It also reported that students educated in Indigenous or minority languages could obtain translated external assessment materials, with exceptions for language and literature examinations. The provisions concerning official EU languages do not extend to Russian. Hungary subsequently dropped its objections to opening the two additional clusters. The October 13 decision moved those policy areas into negotiations, with requirements for alignment and implementation still to be met. A process that began in 2022 Ukraine applied for EU membership in February 2022, days after Russia’s full-scale invasion. It received candidate status that June. EU leaders agreed in December 2023 to begin accession negotiations, which formally opened in June 2024. The Commission describes the negotiations as a process of bringing national law and institutions into line with the EU’s established body of law. Its assessment covers judicial and administrative reforms as well as economic preparedness. The fundamentals cluster addresses core institutions and democratic standards, while external relations concerns alignment of international, trade and defense policies. Under the Commission’s general accession procedures, officials first examine a candidate’s readiness in individual policy fields. The candidate submits negotiating positions, and the EU adopts common positions. Conditions attached to those positions determine the requirements for closing negotiations in each field. Every EU government must be satisfied with a candidate’s progress before an individual chapter can close. The full negotiations conclude only after all chapters have been closed. Membership then requires an accession treaty setting out the terms, transitional arrangements and financial provisions. That treaty needs support from the EU institutions, signatures from the candidate and existing member countries, and ratification under their respective constitutional procedures. The pace of reform determines the length of negotiations; opening talks does not establish an entry date. Economic links already in place Ukraine’s trading relationship with the bloc operates under an association agreement that formally entered into force in September 2017. Its free-trade provisions had applied provisionally since January 2016, and an upgraded trade text entered into force October 29, 2025, according to the Commission’s trade directorate. The directorate puts bilateral goods trade at €68.2 billion in 2025: €21.7 billion in EU imports from Ukraine and €46.5 billion in EU exports to Ukraine. It identifies the EU as Ukraine’s largest goods-trading partner, accounting for around 65 percent of Ukraine’s trade that year. The accession work also proceeds alongside EU wartime assistance. An October 7 payment of €1.24 billion supported purchases of Ukrainian-made drones and missiles, reported by The FINANCIAL . The Commission’s support timeline records that payment separately from the October 13 negotiating decision. Questions and answers How many accession clusters has Ukraine opened? Four of six, following the October 13 opening of the internal-market and competitiveness clusters. What will the task force work on? Reported priorities include interim benchmarks, rule-of-law reforms and anti-corruption requirements. Has Ukraine been given an EU entry date? Not yet. The developments described concern negotiations and reforms. Membership requires completion of the process and an accession treaty approved and ratified by the parties. https://hotnews.ro/rusia-a-vrut-sa-trans.text: Rusia a încercat să transforme yuanul într-un nou dolar adoptând moneda chineză cu o viteză amețitoare după ce forțele sale au invadat Ucraina , iar Occidentul -a impus sancțiuni. Yuanul chinezesc a ajuns să reprezinte aproape jumătate din comerțul exterior al Rusiei, a devenit moneda cu cel mai mare volum de tranzacționare pe piața valutară internă a Moscovei și a depășit dolarul în depozitele bancare. Băncile acordau împrumuturi în yuani, piața obligațiunilor în moneda chineză a crescut cu rate de două cifre, iar moneda a devenit unul dintre principalele elemente din rezervele băncii centrale. Până la mijlocul anului 2024, Rusia crease efectiv un canal suplimentar pentru utilizarea internațională a yuanului. Valoarea exporturilor rusești exprimate în yuani a depășit în mod constant valoarea exporturilor care mergeau direct către China , ceea ce înseamnă că și cumpărătorii din alte regiuni plăteau din ce în ce mai mult către Rusia în yuani. Însă acum, în al cincilea an al războiului, Rusia a abandonat eforturile de a înlocui dolarul cu yuanul, potrivit Bloomberg. În ciuda creșterii comerțului dintre Rusia și China, ponderea yuanului în plățile pentru exporturile rusești a scăzut la 22% în acest an. În comerțul cu Asia, Rusia primește acum ruble pentru 69% din exporturile sale. Experiența Rusiei este un experiment fără precedent care a scos în evidență, în cele din urmă, limitele ambiției președintelui chinez Xi Jinping de a transforma yuanul într-o „monedă puternică” pentru comerțul internațional, piețele financiare și rezervele băncilor centrale, comentează Bloomberg. În același timp, aceasta reamintește că oficialii chinezi au precizat clar că nu urmăresc să facă din yuan un substitut pentru dolar. Schimbarea de poziție a Rusiei a venit după ce băncile chineze au cedat amenințărilor americane cu sancțiuni secundare din cauza războiului din Ucraina. Companiile rusești au fost puternic afectate de când SUA și-au extins semnificativ sancțiunile secundare asupra instituțiilor financiare și companiilor care fac afaceri cu Rusia în iunie 2024. Plățile au fost înghețate sau amânate timp de luni de zile, remitențele au fost returnate, iar cele mai mari instituții financiare din China și-au întrerupt complet relațiile cu contrapartidele rusești. Economia rusă, care se bazase în mare măsură pe yuan, se confrunta cu o lipsă acută de valută. Banca Rusiei a îndemnat în cele din urmă instituțiile de credit să limiteze acordarea de împrumuturi în yuan. Acest fapt demonstrează capacitatea Statelor Unite de a-și impune voința politică – chiar și împotriva celei de-a doua economii mondiale – și subliniază dominația globală a dolarului, notează agenția. Cu toate acestea, renunțarea la yuan a cauzat și alte probleme pentru companiile rusești în ceea ce privește plățile transfrontaliere. Neputând efectua tranzacții direct în moneda chineză, companiile rusești sunt obligate să utilizeze intermediari, țări terțe și rute de plată mai complicate, ceea ce face ca tranzacțiile să fie mai lente, mai scumpe și mai greu de controlat.
